tokenization.rule: parseArgs (src/cli/args.ts:36-79) walks argv left to right; a token NOT starting with '--' is appended to commandPath; a token starting with '--' is a flag token.

equalsForm.rule: --flag=value splits on the FIRST '=' only (assignment.indexOf('=')), so a value may itself contain '=' (e.g. --value=a=b=c -> 'a=b=c'); --flag= yields an empty string value, not boolean true.

spaceSeparatedForm.rule: for a flag not resolved via '=': if the flag name is in CLI_BOOLEAN_FLAGS, it is stored as boolean true and no lookahead occurs. Otherwise: if there is no next token, or the next token itself starts with '--', the flag is ALSO stored as boolean true (implicit presence flag); otherwise the next token is consumed as the flag's string value and the index is advanced past it.
spaceSeparatedForm.note: this lookahead is the ONLY type inference the parser performs for non-boolean flag names; there is no numeric/enum/JSON coercion anywhere in these 4 files.

commandBoundaryDetection.rule: parseArgs calls findCliCommandIndex(argv, commandPaths ?? []) (src/cli/args.ts:39) to find where a pre-command global flag/value run ends and the actual command path begins, so a value like '--environment status' does not get misread as the command 'status'.

knownValueFlagsUnused.fact: findCliCommandIndex accepts an optional 3rd parameter, knownValueFlags, that lets a caller declare specific flags as ALWAYS value-taking (bypassing the generic lookahead heuristic). src/cli/args.ts's parseArgs NEVER passes this 3rd argument (always defaults to []); the only other caller in the pinned checkout, src/main/startup/cli-launch-redirect.ts:129 (desktop launch redirect, not the CLI parser), DOES pass CLI_LAUNCH_VALUE_FLAG_NAMES.
knownValueFlagsUnused.implication: actual CLI argv parsing relies solely on the generic 2-lookahead heuristic in commandPathStartsAt/findCliCommandIndex for disambiguating a value flag from a command-starting token; the knownValueFlags fast path is exercised by tests (src/shared/cli-argument-boundary.test.ts:28-32) but is NOT reachable from the real CLI parse path.

bareDoubleDashNote.fact: a literal '--' token has no argument-terminator meaning anywhere in this contract; it is parsed as an ordinary flag token with an EMPTY flag name (assignment = ''), which is not in CLI_BOOLEAN_FLAGS, so command-boundary lookahead treats it like any other unrecognized flag.

globalFlags.rule: GLOBAL_FLAGS are allowed on EVERY command regardless of that command's own allowedFlags (validateCommandAndFlags: isGlobalFlag = GLOBAL_FLAGS.includes(flag) short-circuits the allowedFlags check).
globalFlags.valueRequiredRule: for pairing-code and environment specifically: if present, the parsed value must be a non-empty string, else validateCommandAndFlags throws invalid_argument 'Flag --<name> requires a value.' -- this applies even to a command whose spec never references these flags, since the check runs unconditionally in the flag-validation loop.
testAnchors: src/cli/args.test.ts:272-283 (allowed on a spec with allowedFlags: [])

booleanFlags.criticalDistinction: CLI_BOOLEAN_FLAGS membership controls ONLY how the token is PARSED (boolean true vs. consuming a value). It does NOT by itself make the flag ALLOWED on a given command. Except for 'help' and 'json' (which are also in GLOBAL_FLAGS and thus always allowed), all other boolean-typed flags must STILL be declared in that specific command's spec.allowedFlags to pass validateCommandAndFlags, exactly like any handler-typed flag. 39 of the 41 declared boolean flags appear in at least one command's allowedFlags in the current 234-command catalog; the remaining 2 ('help','json') never need to appear there because they are global.

repeatableStringFlags.rule: only for flag names in this fixed 2-name set: a second (and later) string-valued occurrence of the SAME flag is appended to the existing value joined by the separator, instead of overwriting it. Non-repeatable string flags (every other name) simply overwrite on a later occurrence -- the last value wins.

conditionallyGlobalPageFlag.rule: supportsBrowserPageFlag(spec.path) (src/cli/args.ts:97-132) computes, per command path, whether 'page' is treated as an ADDITIONAL global-equivalent flag for that command (added into effectiveAllowedFlags and exempted from the allowedFlags check in validateCommandAndFlags), WITHOUT requiring the command's own spec to list 'page' in allowedFlags.

redundantExplicitDeclarations.note: these commands are already page-eligible via supportsBrowserPageFlag, so their explicit 'page' entry in allowedFlags is redundant with (not required for) validation, though it does still surface in that command's own literal allowedFlags list.

handlerTypedFlags.rule: every allowedFlags name that is NOT global, NOT in CLI_BOOLEAN_FLAGS, NOT in REPEATABLE_STRING_FLAGS, and NOT 'page' gets NO parser-level type system beyond the boolean-vs-string lookahead described in spaceSeparatedForm above. These 4 files impose no required/optional/default/enum/numeric constraint on any of them; validateCommandAndFlags only checks NAME membership (is this flag name declared for this command), never a value shape.
handlerTypedFlags.caution: this is the population the task calls out explicitly: 'a flag not in the boolean set is not universally optional or type-validated.' Whatever required/optional/default/type semantics a given handler-typed flag actually has is a per-command HANDLER concern, not a parser concern, and is NOT enumerated per command by this audit (see handlerObligations).

unknownCommand.rule: validateCommandAndFlags (src/cli/args.ts:230-238): if findCommandSpec(specs, parsed.commandPath) returns no match, throws RuntimeClientError('invalid_argument', 'Unknown command: <joined path>', unknownCommandData(specs, parsed.commandPath)).
unknownCommand.suggestionRule: unknownCommandData -> suggestCommands (src/cli/command-suggestion.ts:62-92): candidates are filtered to the SAME depth as the input path, hidden specs are always excluded, destructive specs/aliases are excluded UNLESS the mistyped final token is itself within Levenshtein distance <= 1 (DESTRUCTIVE_INTENT_THRESHOLD) of some destructive verb's final token; remaining candidates within distance <= 3 (SUGGESTION_THRESHOLD) are sorted by (distance, then label) and capped at 3 (MAX_SUGGESTIONS).

unknownFlag.rule: validateCommandAndFlags (src/cli/args.ts:249-261): for each parsed flag, it is accepted iff GLOBAL_FLAGS.includes(flag) OR spec.allowedFlags.includes(flag) OR (flag === 'page' && supportsBrowserPageFlag(spec.path)); otherwise throws RuntimeClientError('invalid_argument', 'Unknown flag --<flag> for command: <path>', unknownFlagData(flag, effectiveAllowedFlags(spec))).
unknownFlag.suggestionRule: unknownFlagData (src/cli/command-suggestion.ts:108-124) sorts the valid-flags list alphabetically for display, ranks suggestions by the same Levenshtein distance<=3/top-3 rule as command suggestions (no destructive-style suppression for flags), and always appends a 'Valid flags: ...' next step even with zero suggestions.

helpResolution.rule: resolveHelpPath (src/cli/args.ts:81-89) has two INDEPENDENT triggers: (1) parsed.commandPath[0] === 'help' (a literal first command token, not a flag) returns the remaining path; (2) else, parsed.flags.has('help') returns the full parsed commandPath unchanged. Neither path is gated by validateCommandAndFlags -- 'help' the flag is global (always allowed) and requires no per-command declaration.
